sources.title: Bibliothèque nationale de France: Les Carolingiens
sources.note: Political chronology: coronation 800, Louis the Pious, Verdun 843, Charles the Fat 884 to 887 and breakup. Do not repeat the handout’s older manuscript dating.

sources.title: Einhard: Life of Charlemagne, translated by Samuel Epes Turner
sources.note: Primary court biography, chapters 19, 22 and 25. Distinguish author’s portrayal of royal family from population-wide practice.

sources.title: UNESCO: Aachen Cathedral
sources.note: Octagonal Carolingian chapel, reused ancient columns, bronze gates and later changes. Present dome mosaics date to 1880 to 1881.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: Carolingian Art
sources.note: Alcuin, scholarly networks, Carolingian minuscule, manuscript and ivory production.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: Gospel Book, 2015.560
sources.note: Circa 825 to 850, probably Metz; ink and opaque watercolor on parchment, modern binding, canon-table cross references.

sources.title: St Gall Abbey Library: Musik im Kloster St. Gallen, 2010
sources.note: Printed page 93: Codex 1092, Reichenau circa 820 for Gozbert; five sewn parchment pieces; dedicatory letter perscrutinare and sollertiam exercere.

sources.title: INRAP: Mérigest, Carré Sénart
sources.note: Ninth-century rural unit: two post-built structures, well, three successive ovens, millstone and iron objects; recycling proposed, not proven.

sources.title: Capitulary for Saxony, translated by D. C. Munro
sources.note: Primary law: article 8 threatens death for refusing baptism; do not mistake prescriptive text for a count of executions.

sources.title: Theodor Schieffer, Neue Deutsche Biographie: Ludwig das Kind
sources.note: 1987 NDB article: six-year-old king in 900, episcopal advisers, death in 911, Raffelstetten customs regulation 903 to 906.

sources.title: Neue Deutsche Biographie: Konrad I
sources.note: Election after Louis the Child’s death in 911; participation of regional elites and conflict over Lotharingia.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: Ottonian Art
sources.note: Otto I’s 936 royal and 962 imperial coronations, court and monastic art, Otto II’s 972 marriage to Theophanu.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art Bulletin: Medieval Sculpture, 800 to 1400
sources.note: Printed page 7: Otto I presenting Magdeburg cathedral, 962 to 968, probably Milan; sixteen surviving plaques and uncertain original furnishing.

sources.title: City of Bad Gandersheim: Town history
sources.note: Women’s religious community, Hrotsvit and classical literary learning; market, mint and toll rights in 990.

sources.title: Paul Derks: scholarly discussion of names and medieval self-description
sources.note: Hrotsvit paragraph and footnote 193 quote drama preface Ego, Clamor Validus Gandeshemensis, with German translation strong voice; references Homeyer edition page 233.

sources.title: St Gall Abbey Library: Töne für die Seele, exhibition catalogue 2025
sources.note: Pages 40 to 41, Hartker Antiphonary, Codices Sangallenses 390 and 391, circa 990 to 1000; five neume scribes and later division of the volume.

sources.title: Municipal museum Königspfalz Tilleda: History
sources.note: Early tenth-century fortification, 972 dower grant to Theophanu, royal charters 974 to 1042; later archaeological interpretations revised.

sources.title: Municipal museum Königspfalz Tilleda: The royal residence
sources.note: Excavations 1935 to 1979; royal residence used intermittently by traveling court; present reconstructed buildings belong to different medieval phases.

sources.title: Theodor Schieffer, Neue Deutsche Biographie: Karolinger
sources.note: 1977 scholarly article, late western dynasty: Eadgifu and Louis IV in England in 923, return 936, Louis V’s death and Hugh Capet’s election 987.

sources.title: Centre des monuments nationaux: History of Cluny Abbey
sources.note: Foundation around 910, William’s villa and agricultural resources, Berno and free election of successors, papal protection and Odo’s 931 authorization.

sources.title: INRAP: Saint-Gilles de Missignac, Aimargues
sources.note: Excavation synthesizes fifth to thirteenth-century settlement; earthen houses, pottery, sickles, weaving weights and milling stones. Assemblage totals span centuries.

sources.title: INRAP: Medieval village discovery, 19 February 2013
sources.note: Early report: major ninth to eleventh-century settlement, church/cemetery, courtyards and storage zones with 450 silos across occupation; not simultaneous households.

sources.title: Alain Busser, IREMI Université de La Réunion: Gerbert et nomogrammes
sources.note: Section 1 distinguishes surviving medieval documents from modern teaching reconstructions; Gerbert’s place-value letter and Richer’s 27-column abacus description.

sources.title: Société de l’histoire de France: Gerbert source bibliography
sources.note: Historical bibliography: studies in Catalonia, teaching at Reims from 972, papacy in 999.

sources.title: Université Paul-Valéry Montpellier: Serments de Strasbourg
sources.note: Romance oath transcription and translation, opening Pro Deo amur et pro christian poblo. Do not repeat page’s erroneous dating of Nithard.

sources.title: Corpus Eve: Les Serments de Strasbourg dans la chronique de Nithard
sources.note: 2018 philological study, paragraphs 41 to 42: BnF Latin 9768 copied late tenth or early eleventh century, not autograph; ninth-century original lost.

sources.title: Bibliothèque nationale de France: Monnaies et médailles
sources.note: Carolingian coins, eighth to tenth centuries: predominantly silver, crosses, monograms, temple images and mint names.

sources.title: Cambridge University Press: A Concise History of Belgium, Austrian Netherlands
sources.note: Scholarly chapter summary: eighteenth-century Austrian rule from 1713 to 1794; distinguish dynastic provinces from modern Belgium.

sources.title: Belgian State Archives: Grand Conseil de Malines inventory
sources.note: Historical introduction: Fleurus 26 June 1794, French occupation, annexation 1 October 1795 and displaced institutions.

sources.title: KBR: The Ferraris map
sources.note: Original maps 1770 to 1778, 275 sheets, including Austrian Netherlands and Liège; digitization description.

sources.title: KBR: De grote atlas van Ferraris
sources.note: Historical map use and detail, cabinet scale 1:11,520; streets, settlements, gardens; not a modern border census.

sources.title: Académie royale de Belgique: Institutional history
sources.note: Society 1769, Maria Theresa’s charter 16 December 1772, sciences and belles-lettres. Do not reproduce page’s anachronistic Austria-Hungary label.

sources.title: KBR: Palais de Charles de Lorraine
sources.note: Governor 1744 to 1780, palace construction from 1757, rotunda marble samples and art/science interests.

sources.title: City of Brussels: Manneken-Pis, 400 years press dossier
sources.note: Chronology: festival costumes attested 1720, Louis XV’s 1747 costume after soldiers’ attempted theft, first known dresser 1756.

sources.title: Wallonia heritage service: Collège royal Marie-Thérèse, Herve
sources.note: Royal college founded 9 March 1777, opened 1 January 1778 after Jesuit suppression; requisitioned by French in 1794.

sources.title: Belgian State Archives: Commission royale des études inventory
sources.note: Historical introduction, numbered 1777 reforms: competitive teacher recruitment open to lay/clergy, inspection, curriculum and tuition changes.

sources.title: Museum Plantin-Moretus: English visitor guide
sources.note: Printed page 24: Maria Theresia Borrekens, thirteen children, leadership after husband’s 1768 death for 29 years; business difficulties.

sources.title: Museum Plantin-Moretus: Naar school met de Moretussen
sources.note: January 1776 French New Year letter from fifteen-year-old Frans Jozef at Mons boarding school to grandmother; distinguish earlier 1695 anecdote.

sources.title: STAM Ghent city museum: Optical print of Rasphuis, object 01050
sources.note: Print dated 1800 depicts prison built 1772 to 1775 under Maria Theresa; prisoners rasped dyewood. Image postdates Austrian government.

sources.title: KBR: Le manifeste du peuple brabançon
sources.note: Catalogued primary publication, Henri Charles Nicolas van der Noot, 1789, [2], 26 pages; title as short French language witness.

sources.title: Wallonia historical atlas: États-Belgiques-Unis, 1790
sources.note: Different provincial responses to 1789 revolt, rival opposition groups and temporary union in 1790.

sources.title: Haus der Geschichte Österreich: Die Republik Österreich
sources.note: Republic founded 1918, 1920 constitution, authoritarian rupture 1934 and Nazi annexation 1938.

sources.title: Haus der Geschichte Österreich: Human rights, stop 3
sources.note: Women’s 1919 vote, first eight female deputies; Burjan and Boschek’s 1920 domestic-servant legislation, rest and holiday rights.

sources.title: Austrian legal information system: Federal Constitutional Law, Article 1
sources.note: Primary German legal text: Österreich ist eine demokratische Republik. Ihr Recht geht vom Volk aus.

sources.title: Wiener Wohnen: History of municipal housing
sources.note: Municipal building after 1919; light, air, in-flat WCs/water, kindergartens, baths and gardens; Karl-Marx-Hof 1927 to 1930.

sources.title: Wiener Wohnen: Wiener Gemeindebau guide
sources.note: Karl-Marx-Hof chapter: two bathhouses with tubs/showers and communal laundries; apartments had water points, not standard private bathrooms.

sources.title: Mauthausen Memorial: Concentration camp 1938 to 1945
sources.note: Camp established 1938 after annexation; forced construction/quarry labor, persecution, mass murder, US liberation 5 May 1945.

sources.title: Haus der Geschichte Österreich: Declaration of Independence
sources.note: 27 April 1945 provisional government, 1920 constitution, western recognition in October, November elections; victim myth and responsibility.

sources.title: Austrian Parliament: State Treaty and neutrality
sources.note: Treaty signed 15 May 1955, entered force 27 July; neutrality is separate constitutional law of 26 October 1955.

sources.title: Austrian education ministry: Schulbuchaktion
sources.note: Schoolbook scheme introduced 1972 to assist families and access to educational materials; do not assert uninterrupted absence of all co-payments.

sources.title: Austrian social ministry: Eltern-Kind-Pass
sources.note: Mutter-Kind-Pass introduced 1974; records pregnancy/childhood preventive examinations, renamed Eltern-Kind-Pass in 2024.

sources.title: Austrian Federal Chancellery: 1995
sources.note: 1994 referendum and EU accession on 1 January 1995.

sources.title: Nobel Foundation: Anton Zeilinger, facts
sources.note: 2022 shared physics prize for experiments with entangled photons, Bell inequalities and quantum information; Vienna affiliations.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Existing thin card is deliberately upgraded. Supersede old entity in data/research/regions/europe-ancient-medieval/evidence.json and its accepted review when integrating. Topology for 800 is broad Frankish/Italian realm; 900 labeled polygon is largely middle/Italian territory, not a still-unified empire. 1000 is map coverage, not fall date.
Distinct decoded world900 polygons and 900 to 1000 index coverage. Do not merge either into Carolingian Empire. East includes non-Carolingian rulers; West includes the Capetian succession in 987.

Index alias Republic of Austria; coverage starts1920. Decoded polygons occur1920 to 1938 and1945 to 2020. This is modern republic, not Habsburg Austria. Narrative includes1918 to 1919 context and1938 to 1945 interruption.
Index1783 to 1815; decoded1783 and1800 polygons persist unchanged across1794 conquest/1795 annexation. Preserve map dates as coverage but explain actual ending.
